segments.text:
These lines continue the function `section4` that starts at line 24. The view was added after the numbers were seen.
- `allla`: every launch line of `launches.txt` in the run folders of rows L-1 to L-4. It also holds the launch lines of processes of these folders whose csv files the sheet does not use.
- The loop visits each process of these rows. These are the processes whose csv files the sheet uses (`v['secs']`). `la` is the launch line of the process.
- `prev`: the process of `allla` that ended last at or before this launch, by the time of its rc line. It may lie in another run folder. It is `None` when no process ended before.
- `gap`: the seconds from the rc line of `prev` to the launch line of this process. Both lines give whole seconds.
- `first`: true when this launch is the earliest launch of its own run folder.
segments.heading: Section 4.2 view: the 8000 MT/s pool by start state

segments.text:
The processes are split by the 1-minute load average of their launch line (`load1`).
- `idle`: load below 1.0. `busy`: load 1.0 or above.
- Line 535 stops the build unless each group has a process and every `idle` process is the first of its run folder.
- Lines 536 to 538 stop the build unless two things hold for every `busy` process. `prev` ran with `--threads 120` and `--cpus 0-63,64-119`. The process was launched more than 0 s and at most 30 s after `prev` ended.
- This check reads the arguments of `prev` only. It does not read the name of a binary. All launch lines of `allla` come from the run folders of the bwx12 rows.

`grp` returns the records of rows L-1 to L-4 for one kernel and position whose process is in the given group. A process is matched by its row name and its tag.
- `Io`, `Bo`: oldread at position 0 of the groups `idle` and `busy`.
- `Ia`, `Ba`: asmread at position 1 of the two groups.
- Line 541 stops the build unless the two groups together have as many intervals as the pool lists `P12o` and `P12a`. So the split leaves out no interval of the pool.

Helpers for the table and the text below.
- `gaps_`: the `gap` values of the `busy` processes in seconds, sorted.
- `loads`: the sorted loads at launch of a group.
- `names`: the processes of a group as text, each as row name and tag.
- `lsrc`: the `[RefN]` labels of the `launches.txt` files of a group, each file once.

Writes the opening sentences of the view and its table. The sentences say that the view is not part of the fixed rules. The table has one row per group.
- Its columns are the group, the processes, the load at launch, the work before the launch, n, the lowest to highest oldread rate, the lowest to highest asmread rate, and the source files.
- Here n is taken from the oldread list of the group. No line tests that the asmread list of the group has the same n. In the present data it has the same n in both groups.
- The row of the `busy` group prints the lowest and the highest load, and the shortest and the longest `gap`.
- Loads are printed with 2 decimal places, gaps as whole seconds.

`aIo`, `aBo`, `aIa` and `aBa` are the ranges of the four lists (lowest rate, highest rate, median, counts). Each `need` stops the build when its condition is false.
- Line 557: the lowest oldread rate of the `busy` group is above the highest oldread rate of the `idle` group.
- Line 558: the asmread ranges of the two groups overlap.
- Line 559: `kLB` compares oldread of part L (`L72o`) with `Bo`. `kLaB` compares asmread of part L (`L72a`) with `Ba`.
- Lines 560 and 561: part L lies below `Bo` for oldread and above `Ba` for asmread, both without overlap.
- Line 562: the oldread range of F72d12 overlaps the range of the `idle` group. The oldread range of control I overlaps it too.

`c['byst']` keeps the view for later sections of the sheet. The values are stored without rounding.
- `near`: the lowest oldread rate of `Bo` minus the highest oldread rate of part L, in GB/s. It is `kLB['dist']` with the opposite sign.
- `near_pct`: `near` divided by the lowest oldread rate of `Bo`, times 100. Unit: percent.
- `asm_near`: the lowest asmread rate of part L minus the highest asmread rate of `Ba`, in GB/s.
- In the present FACTS.md `near` is 4.27 GB/s. That is 0.9 % of 468.56 GB/s [Ref4].

`Ctags` holds the tags of the part C processes, taken from the oldread records `C72o`. `Cprev` holds, for each of them, the step that ran directly before it (`evd[t]['prev']`). The steps are the part A folders and the bwx12 processes of go.sh and go2.sh, in time order. The build stops unless all of these hold:
- Every step before is a bwx12 process of part L or of part C.
- Every part C process was launched more than 0 s and at most 30 s after that step ended. The field `gap_s` holds this time.
- All part C processes have the same `gap_s`.
segments.heading: Part C in the start-state view

segments.text:
`Cf0` holds the oldread intervals of part C at position 0. `Cf0tags` holds the tags of their processes. The build stops unless all of these hold:
- Every oldread interval of part C at position 2 ran directly after kernel `read`.
- Positions 0 and 2 together hold every oldread interval of part C.
- Every process with oldread at position 0 has the spec name `cfwd` in `D['X']`. This name comes from a fixed list in `facts_data.py`, not from the launch line [Ref2]. `build_facts.py` compares the launch line of each process with its spec file in its check `args` [Ref3].

Three comparisons of oldread: all of part C against `Bo` (`kCB`), position 0 of part C against `Bo` (`kCfB`), and all of part C against `Io` (`kCIo`). The build stops unless part C lies below `Bo` without overlap in the first two, and overlaps `Io` in the third. `c['partC_view']` stores the result:
- `all`, `cf0`: the ranges of all oldread intervals of part C and of its oldread intervals at position 0.
- `near`, `near_cf0`: the lowest rate of `Bo` minus the highest rate of part C, in GB/s. `near` uses all oldread intervals, `near_cf0` only position 0.
- `near_pct`: `near` divided by the lowest rate of `Bo`, times 100.
- `gap`, `prev`, `loads`: the `gap_s` of the first part C process, the tags of the steps before, and the sorted loads at launch (`Cload`).
- `both`: the range of oldread over part L and part C together. The text below prints only its counts.
- In the present FACTS.md `near` is 0.42 GB/s and `near_cf0` is 0.73 GB/s [Ref4].

The same kind of start state in rows R0 and R0b (binary bwx11). The loop repeats the search of lines 525 to 532 with the launch lines of the run folders of these two rows.
- A process enters `busy11` when two things hold. The process before it ran with `--threads 120` and `--cpus 0-63,64-119`. That process ended more than 0 s and at most 30 s before the launch.
- No load value is tested here. Line 534 tests one for the pool.
- `B11o`: the oldread intervals at position 0 of the `busy11` processes.
segments.heading: The same start state in the other-binary rows

segments.text:
`bx0v` holds oldread at position 0 of the runner bwx rows B7a, B7b, C3a and C3b. `prev120` holds one entry per used process of these rows: the `-- step` line (the header line) of the process directly before it in the same csv file. The check in lines 600 to 602 tests no time gap, no load and no `--cpus` list. The build stops unless all of these hold:
- `busy11` is not empty.
- `prev120` has as many entries as `bx0v` has processes, and no entry is missing.
- Every entry names the binary `bwx` and holds `--threads 120`.

- `aB11`, `aBx0`: the ranges of `B11o` and `bx0v`.
- `allo`: every oldread record at 8000 MT/s with 12 modules, of every row and every position. `low_o` is the record with the lowest rate.
- Line 606 stops the build unless the oldread range of part C overlaps `aB11` and overlaps `aBx0`.
- Lines 607 and 608 stop the build unless two things hold. The highest oldread rate of part L is below the rate of `low_o`. The binaries of `allo` are exactly bwx12, bwx11 and bwx.
- `c['byst_other']` and `c['byst']['L_hi']` keep these values for later sections. `bx0_load` is the lowest and the highest load at launch of `bx0v`.
- In the present FACTS.md `allo` has 124 intervals [Ref4].

Writes nine list items of the view. Every number comes from the values above.
- Items 1 and 2 (lines 612 to 617): the two oldread groups at 8000 MT/s, and part L against the `busy` group. Item 2 says how many seconds after part A part L started. This number is the `gap_s` of process T72L1 only. The last number is `near` of line 489, the distance against the whole pool.
- Items 3 to 6 (lines 619 to 637): part C against the two groups, from `c['partC_view']` and the ranges of the groups. Here `near_pct` is printed with 2 decimal places.
- Item 7 (lines 638 and 639): the oldread ranges of F72d12, of control I and of the `idle` group.
- Item 7 calls F72d12 and control I rows that were launched at a load below 1.0. Line 898 tests this load for control I. No `need` call of this file tests it for F72d12. The present load at launch of F72d12 is 0.34 [Ref4].
- Item 8 (lines 640 and 641): asmread of part L against `Ba`.
- Item 9 (line 642): the 8000 MT/s rows show a higher oldread rate after 120-thread work, not a lower one. The check in line 557 stops the build when the data do not show this.

Writes the limits of the view.
- `l11`, `g11`: the sorted loads at launch and the distinct `gap` values of the `busy11` processes. `lbx`: the sorted loads at launch of `bx0v`.
- Lines 646 to 655: the `busy` group holds bwx12 processes only. Against the bwx11 processes and the bwx processes with that kind of start state part C overlaps. The item prints both ranges and the highest oldread rate of part C.
- Lines 656 to 659: the highest oldread rate of part L is below every interval of `allo`. The item prints the number of intervals of `allo`, and the rate, row and tag of `low_o`.
- Lines 660 to 664: four limits. They are the work before the launch, the interval lengths and counter events of `Bo`, the position of oldread in part C, and one boot per memory speed. The item prints the interval lengths of `Bo`, and how many oldread intervals of part C are at position 2.
- Line 665: the measurement that would show why the old read kernel was lower in part L (`H1_MEAS`).

Record lists for the two tables below.
- `Cf`, `Cr`: oldread of part C at position 0 and at position 2.
- `bx0`, `bx7`: oldread of the runner bwx rows B7a, B7b, C3a and C3b at position 0 and at position 7.
- `scm` keeps the records of the processes that ran with `--start common`.
- Line 675 stops the build unless every record of part C ran with `--start common`.
- `nsc`: the number of processes with `--start common` among `bx0`. The labels of lines 686, 952, 960 and 998 and the text of line 1028 print this number for other lists of runner bwx too: `bx7`, `bx1` (line 950), `bx6` (line 958) and `bx2` (line 975). No line tests it for these lists. In the present FACTS.md each of them has 12 such processes [Ref4].
segments.heading: Section 4.2: old read kernel in part C

segments.text:
Writes the range table of oldread. Each row gives n, the lowest to highest rate and the median of one record list.
- Part C: all oldread intervals, position 0 only, and position 2 only.
- The label of position 2 names the spec `crev`. Line 574 tests the spec name for position 0 only. In the present data the processes with oldread at position 2 are T72C2 and T72C4, the two crev processes.
- 8000 MT/s rows of the fixed list: L-1 alone, the pool L-1 to L-4, and the pool with rows R0 and R0b.
- The row of L-1 alone says `oldread at position 0`. The code selects `l1o` by row and kernel, without a position (line 480). This file does not test the position of these records. In the present facts.json both records of `l1o` are at position 0.
- Runner bwx at 8000 MT/s: position 0 and position 7. Each of these two lists is shown twice: with all processes, and with the `--start common` processes only.
- The labels call position 7 of runner bwx `oldread directly after read`. The code selects `bx7` by position. This file does not test the kernel before of these rows. In the present facts.json `kernel_before` is `read` for every record of `bx7`.

`cmps` runs six range tests and returns their table. It also stores each test in `V['q2_rows']`.
- All oldread intervals of part C against L-1 alone, against the pool L-1 to L-4, and against the pool with R0 and R0b. Only the test of all oldread intervals against the pool L-1 to L-4 has `decides` = True. So only this one of the six tests gets a wording.
- Position 0 of part C against the pool L-1 to L-4 and against runner bwx at position 0.
- Position 2 of part C against runner bwx at position 7.
- `kC1` and `kCall` (line 687) repeat two of the tests for the check in line 699.

Writes the result of the deciding test. `cCo` is the comparison of all oldread intervals of part C with the pool L-1 to L-4. `facts_text.py` made it [Ref1].
- The text prints its wording, both n, and the width of the 8000 MT/s range: (highest - lowest) / lowest x 100, with 1 decimal place.
- Line 699 stops the build unless part C also overlaps L-1 alone and the pool with R0 and R0b.

`lowC` holds the oldread intervals of part C whose rate is below the lowest rate of the pool L-1 to L-4. The text prints their number, the number of all oldread intervals of part C, and the tags of their processes. The next item repeats the result of the start-state view: the range of `Bo` and `near` of `c['partC_view']`. The last item has fixed words.

Writes the title and three opening items. This section works on `pa3`, the six cells that `facts_text.py` prepared [Ref1].
- A cell is one binary with one load-only kernel in one round.
- From the rerun a cell holds session 1 only. Sessions 2 and 3 of part A are left out of this section.
- `cellt` prints the intervals of one table cell: each rate with 2 decimal places and its pass count in brackets.
segments.heading: Section 4.3: new read kernel in part A (rule V3)

segments.text:
The wording of rule V3 for one cell `x`. The 8000 MT/s range of the cell (`b80`) spans the intervals of rows A-1 and A-2 of the same binary, kernel and round. `facts_text.py` has counted how many of the 3 intervals of session 1 lie above its highest rate, below its lowest rate, or inside it [Ref1].
- All 3 inside: `inside the range of the 8000 MT/s runs; no difference shown`, and no distance.
- All 3 above: `outside (above)`. The distance text gives the smallest and the largest of the 3 distances to the highest rate of `b80`, in GB/s.
- All 3 below: `outside (below)`, with the distances to the lowest rate of `b80`.
- Any other case: the three counts and every distance.
- No percent and no median are computed here.

Adds the table row of the cell, and its entry in `V['q2_rows']` for facts.json. The entry holds the wording of lines 724 to 732 and `decides` = True.
- `lo_7200`, `hi_7200`: the lowest and the highest rate of the 3 intervals of session 1. `n_7200` = 3 and `processes_7200` = 1 are fixed numbers in the code.
- `scope_8000`: the rows that have a process for this cell (A-1, A-2 or both) and the round.
- `lo_8000`, `hi_8000`, `n_8000`, `processes_8000`: taken from `b80`.
- `overlap`: true when at least one of the 3 intervals lies inside `b80`. This is not the range test of `compare`.
- `distance_GBps`: the smallest distance above `b80`, rounded to 3 decimal places. It is 0 when no interval lies above, also for a cell that lies below.
- Line 744 copies the two keys `row_7200` and `scope_8000` into the label fields.

Writes the table of the six cells. Line 748 stops the build unless all 3 intervals of session 1 lie above the 8000 MT/s range in every cell. So in a build that finishes, every cell has the wording `outside (above)`. Its `distance_GBps` is the lowest rate of session 1 minus the highest rate of `b80`.

Three medians of `bw_new read`, each over rounds 1 and 2 together.
- `s1new`: session 1 of part A. `a1n`, `a2n`: rows A-1 and A-2.
- Lines 752 and 753 stop the build unless two things hold. A-1 and A-2 have the same n (intervals, processes, boots). Each of the three lists holds rounds 1 and 2.
- `med` is the median of `GBps`. For an even number of values it is the mean of the two middle values.
- The text prints the two 8000 MT/s medians, their distance, the median of session 1 and its distance to each of them.
- Line 761 stops the build unless the smaller of these two distances is larger than the distance between the two 8000 MT/s medians.
- In the present FACTS.md the medians are 289.54 GB/s (A-1), 304.43 GB/s (A-2) and 330.34 GB/s (session 1) [Ref4].

Pass counts of the intervals of the table.
- `p72`: the distinct pass counts of the session 1 intervals of all cells, sorted. `p80`: the same for rows A-1 and A-2.
- `n80`: the number of 8000 MT/s intervals of the table. `n600`: how many of them have the lowest pass count of `p80`.
- The text prints these values. It then states that the whole-pass stop moves the rate together with the pass count. So part A cannot give the size of a change.

Writes the limit of this comparison: session 1, row A-1 and row A-2 started from different states. `a1la` is the first process of row A-1. The text prints its load at launch, a text on the work before row A-2 (`c['a2pre_txt']`), and the load at the launch of the first process of row A-2.

`full` = 64 x 6 + 56 x 5 = 664 passes. The code has no comment on the factors. The numbers fit 64 threads with 6 passes each plus 56 threads with 5 passes each. Rule V3 states that a thread faster than 2.684 GB/s runs a sixth pass in the 0.5 s interval [Ref5].
- `same` keeps the intervals with 663 or 664 passes (`full - 1` or `full`).
- Every interval with another pass count is left out of this view.
- The opening text (lines 778 and 779) says that this view is not part of rule V3. It says that the view was added while the sheet was built.
segments.heading: Section 4.3 view: equal pass count

segments.text:
One table row per cell. `s72` holds the session 1 intervals with 663 or 664 passes. `s80` holds those of rows A-1 and A-2 together.
- `k` is `compare(s72, s80)` when both lists have an interval. If not, `k` is `None` and the two last columns show `-`.
- The 7200 MT/s column prints the range of `s72` (or its one value) and n. An empty list prints `no such interval`.
- The 8000 MT/s column prints the range of `s80`, n, and the number of intervals per row. When `s80` is empty, it prints `no such interval`, the number of all 8000 MT/s intervals of the cell, and their distinct pass counts.
- The distance column prints `0` for an overlap. If not, it prints `k['dist']` in GB/s with the Python format `%+.2f`.

Checks and text of this view.
- `r1`, `r2`: the cells of round 1 and of round 2. `r1all`: all 8000 MT/s intervals of the round 1 cells.
- Line 803 stops the build unless two things hold. No round 1 cell has an 8000 MT/s interval with 663 or 664 passes. All intervals of `r1all` have the same pass count.
- `both`: the round 2 cells that have a comparison. Lines 805 and 806 stop the build unless there is at least one, and session 1 lies above without overlap in each.
- `none2`: the round 2 cells without a comparison. The text names them.
- The text says that the cells of `none2` have no such 8000 MT/s interval. A cell has no comparison when `s72` or `s80` is empty. The code does not test which of the two is empty. In the present FACTS.md the one such cell is `bw_old asmread`, and its 8000 MT/s list is the empty one [Ref4].
- The last item prints how many of the round 2 intervals at 8000 MT/s this view uses.

`half` = 120 x 0.005 = 0.6 GB/s. The csv column `per_thread_avg_GBps` is rounded to 0.01 GB/s. So its rounding error is at most 0.005 GB/s, and 120 times the column is exact to 0.6 GB/s.
- `av` returns the values of this column for a record list.
- `span` prints a list of numbers as one value when all are equal. If not, it prints the lowest to the highest value.
segments.heading: Section 4.3 view: 120 x per-thread average (est.)

segments.text:
One table row per cell. `s1`, `a1` and `a2` hold the per-thread averages of session 1, row A-1 and row A-2. `b` joins `a1` and `a2`.
- `est`: 120 x (lowest value of `s1` - highest value of `b`). It is the distance of the nearest ends by the estimate, in GB/s.
- `agg`: the smallest value of `x['above']`. It is the lowest `aggregate_GBps` of session 1 minus the highest one of rows A-1 and A-2 in the same round.
- `above`: true when every value of `s1` is above every value of `b`.
- The table prints the averages with 2 decimal places and 120 x average with 1 decimal place. It prints `est` with the format `%+.1f` and `agg` with `%+.2f`.

Line 839 stops the build unless `above` is true in every cell. `larger` holds the cells where `est` is greater than `agg`. `smaller` holds the other cells. Line 842 stops the build unless `agg` - `est` is at most 2 x `half` = 1.2 GB/s in every cell of `smaller`.

Check of the estimate against measured thread rates. A1.csv (row A-2) was written with the option `--per-thread`. It holds one row per thread and interval.
- The loop visits every interval of every process of A1.csv. It does not select a kernel. The file holds read kernels and write kernels.
- `rows_` holds the thread rates of the interval. Line 848 stops the build unless there are 120.
- `chk_max`: the largest absolute difference between the sum of the 120 thread rates and 120 x `per_thread_avg_GBps`, over all intervals. `chk_n` counts the intervals.
- Line 851 stops the build unless `chk_max` is at most 1.2 GB/s. The line adds 1e-9 GB/s to this limit for floating-point error.
- In the present FACTS.md: 36 intervals, largest difference 0.66 GB/s [Ref4].

Writes five list items and stores the list `tr` in `c['thr']`.
- Item 1: every per-thread average of session 1 lies above those of the 8000 MT/s processes. Line 839 checks it.
- Item 2: in how many cells `est` is larger than `agg`. For the cells of `smaller` it prints `agg` - `est` with 2 decimal places.
- Item 3: the result of the A1.csv check. It prints `chk_n` and `chk_max`.
- Items 4 and 5: what the estimate shows, and which measurement is missing.
Writes the title and two opening items. The first says that asmread is used in place of the new read kernel. The second says that F72d12 and control I are separate rows in every range test.
segments.heading: Section 4.4: asmread in part L

segments.text:
Writes the range table of asmread. Each row gives n, the lowest to highest rate and the median of one record list.
- Part L (`L72a`).
- Each of the rows L-1 to L-4 at position 1, and their pool (`P12a`).
- Rows R0 and R0b at position 1, and the pool with them (`PALLa`).
- X2d12, F72d12 (`F72a`) and control I (`I72a`).
- The title in line 872 says `position 1, directly after oldread`. The code selects `L72a`, `F72a`, `I72a` and `x2a` (asmread of row X2d12, line 473) by row and kernel, without a position. This file does not test the position or the kernel before of these four lists. In the present facts.json every record of them has position 1 and `kernel_before` oldread.

`cmps` runs nine range tests: part L, F72d12 and control I, each against the three scopes of `sc_a` (line 482).
- The scopes are L-1 alone, the pool L-1 to L-4, and the pool with R0 and R0b.
- Only the pool L-1 to L-4 decides. So three tests get a wording.
- `notes` adds the text of `STANDIN` to the three facts.json entries of part L.

Checks for the text below.
- Line 888: asmread of part L overlaps neither L-1 alone nor the pool with R0 and R0b. This line does not test which range is higher. `facts_text.py` tests that part L lies above the pool L-1 to L-4 [Ref1].
- Line 889: control I lies above the pool L-1 to L-4 without overlap (`cIa`).
- Lines 890 to 892: `kF1` and `kI1` compare F72d12 and control I with L-1 alone. Each must lie above it without overlap.
- Line 893 keeps the two comparisons in `c`.

Start states of L-1 and of control I.
- `l1la`: the launch line of the L-1 process a6456. `Ila`: the launch lines of the control I processes.
- `Igap`: for each control I process, the seconds since the step before it ended.
- `Iref`: the `[RefN]` labels of the `launches.txt` files of control I. Line 1175 uses it.

The build stops unless all of these hold:
- The 1-minute load is below 1.0 for L-1 and for every control I process.
- The 5-minute load of every control I process is above 1.0.
- The 5-minute and the 15-minute load of L-1 are below 1.0.
- Every `Igap` is above 60 s.

Writes three list items.
- Part L: the wording and the distance of `cLa` (part L against the pool L-1 to L-4), and both n.
- Control I: the wording and the distance of `cIa`, the distance against L-1 alone (`kI1`), both n, the three load averages of L-1, and the `Igap` values.
- F72d12: its load at launch, and whether its range overlaps the pool (`cFa`). When it does not overlap L-1 alone, the text adds the distance `kF1['dist']`.

`hwc['P12a_wo']` is the pool `P12a` without its lowest interval. That interval has two hardware error records inside it (lines 297 to 303). `wo` is the range of this smaller pool. Lines 918 to 920 stop the build unless all of these hold:
- Part L and control I each lie above this pool without overlap.
- F72d12 overlaps it, and the whole range of F72d12 lies inside `wo`.
- The highest rate of `wo` equals the highest rate of the full pool.
segments.heading: Section 4.4: the pool without the interval with error records

segments.text:
Writes the item on the hardware error records.
- It prints the rate, row, tag and round of the removed interval (`low_a`).
- It prints the range of the pool without it, its width in GB/s (highest - lowest), its width in percent of its lower end, and n.
- The count `2 corrected records` is typed in the template. Line 291 tests the count. Line 245 tests the severity. Lines 298 to 300 test that the interval with these records is `low_a`.
- The last item (line 930) has fixed words.

Writes the title and three items for kernel `read`. They state that bwx12 never ran this kernel at 8000 MT/s (`NO_READ`). So the rows of runner bwx below come from another binary. They are not a like-for-like baseline.
segments.heading: Section 4.5: kernel read in part C

segments.text:
Rows of the range table of kernel `read`. Part C is grouped by the kernel that ran directly before (rule V2).
- `Rao`: read of part C directly after oldread. `Raa`: read of part C directly after asmread.
- Shown with `Rao`: read at position 1 of each of the rows B7a, B7b, C3a and C3b, and their pool `bx1`. Then the pool with the `--start common` processes only, and rows B5a and B5b.
- Shown with `Raa`: read at position 6 of the same four rows, their pool `bx6`, and the pool with the `--start common` processes only.
- The row labels call position 1 `after oldread` and position 6 `after asmread`.
- For the bwx rows the code selects by position. This file does not test the kernel before of these rows. In the present facts.json `kernel_before` is oldread for every record of `bx1` and for every read record at position 1 of rows B5a and B5b. It is asmread for every record of `bx6`.
- The labels of `Rao` and `Raa` add `cfwd, position 1` and `crev, position 1`. No line of this file tests these parts of the labels. In the present facts.json every record of `Rao` is at position 1 of a cfwd.csv file. Every record of `Raa` is at position 1 of a crev.csv file.

`k1` compares `Rao` with `bx1`. `k6` compares `Raa` with `bx6`.
- `q2row` stores both tests in `V['q2_rows']` with `decides` = False and the note `NO_READ`. So they carry no wording.
- The text prints each distance in GB/s. A positive `dist` prints as above the highest value of the bwx pool. A negative `dist` prints as below its lowest value.
- A `dist` of 0 prints as `inside its range`. `dist` is 0 for every overlap, also when only a part of the two ranges overlaps.
- In the present FACTS.md both distances are positive: 5.60 GB/s and 3.11 GB/s [Ref4].

Two differences of the bwx reference.
- `cnt`: the distinct pairs of row name and `count` in the records of rows B7a, B7b, C3a and C3b. The text prints them. `count=1` means that the run read core counters.
- The words `Part C used bwx12 with counters` are template text. No line of this file tests the field `count` of the part C records. In the present facts.json `count` is 1 for every record of part C.
- `allp`: one record per process of these rows. `noff` counts the processes with `--start offset`. Line 974 stops the build unless `noff` + `nsc` is the number of all processes and `noff` is above 0.
- `bx2`: asmread at position 2 of the bwx rows.
- `same_ends`: true when the lowest and the highest rate of `bx1`, `bx2` and `bx6` stay the same with the `--start common` processes only. It selects one of two sentences.
- The first sentence also says `the medians change`. The code does not test this part. In the present FACTS.md each of the three medians changes [Ref4]. The last item (lines 983 and 984) has fixed words on decision (p).

Kernel asmread of part C, in three groups by the kernel that ran directly before.
- `Aao`: after oldread. `Aar`: after read. `Aaf`: asmread as the first interval of the process.
- The range table shows the three groups, L-1 alone, the pool L-1 to L-4 (`P12a`) and the pool with R0 and R0b (`PALLa`).
- It also shows asmread at position 2 of runner bwx (`bx2`), with all processes and with the `--start common` processes only. The records of rows B7a, B7b, C3a and C3b also hold asmread at position 5. In the present facts.json their `kernel_before` is `asmread2`, another kernel of runner bwx. No table row and no range test of section 4.5 uses these records.
- The labels call position 2 of runner bwx `asmread after read`. The code selects `bx2` by position. This file does not test the kernel before of these rows. In the present facts.json `kernel_before` is `read` for every record of `bx2`.
- The labels of the three groups also name the spec and the round, for example `crev, round 1, position 0`. The check in lines 999 to 1001 tests the positions of the three groups. No line of this file tests their specs or rounds. In the present facts.json they are as the labels say.
- The row of L-1 alone says `asmread at position 1 (after oldread)`. The code selects `l1a` by row and kernel, without a position (line 480). The check in lines 999 to 1001 tests `PALLa`, not `l1a`. In the present facts.json both records of `l1a` are at position 1 with `kernel_before` oldread.
segments.heading: Section 4.5: kernel asmread in part C

segments.text:
Stops the build unless the positions are as the labels say.
- `Aao` and `Aaf`: position 0.
- `Aar`: position 2.
- Every interval of `PALLa`: position 1, directly after oldread.

`m_k` and `m_0` build scope labels. A label says in what an 8000 MT/s list matches the part C group: the kernel before, the position, or neither. `cmps` runs six range tests.
- `Aao` against L-1 alone, against the pool L-1 to L-4, and against the pool with R0 and R0b. These lists match in the kernel before, not in the position. Only the pool L-1 to L-4 decides.
- `Aaf` against the pool L-1 to L-4. It matches in neither.
- `Aar` against the pool L-1 to L-4 (it matches in neither) and against `bx2`.
- The five tests without `decides` are printed without a wording.

`kAao` repeats the deciding test: `Aao` against `P12a`.
- Line 1016 stops the build unless `Aao` also overlaps neither L-1 alone nor the pool with R0 and R0b. This line does not test which range is higher. Line 1351 tests it for the pool L-1 to L-4.
- The text prints the wording, both n and the tags of the processes of `Aao`.
- `c['kAao']` and `c['Aao']` keep the test for the short version in section 0.
- The two last items have fixed words.

Rule V2 point 5: which of the two conditions of kernel `read` is the lower one.
- 8000 MT/s, runner bwx: `med(bx6) - med(bx1)`, the median of read at position 6 minus the median of read at position 1, in GB/s. The same with the `--start common` processes only.
- 7200 MT/s, part C: `med(Raa) - med(Rao)`.
- The text also prints the number and the tags of the processes of `Raa`.
- Line 1032 stops the build unless the 7200 MT/s difference is positive and the ranges of `Raa` and `Rao` overlap.
- These lines do not test the sign of the two 8000 MT/s differences. In the present FACTS.md both are positive: 10.66 GB/s and 12.29 GB/s [Ref4].

`kAA` compares `Aao` with `Aar`, both of part C at 7200 MT/s. Line 1034 stops the build unless asmread after oldread lies above asmread after read without overlap.
- The text prints each rate of `Aao`, the range of `Aar` and the distance in GB/s.
- The text ends with the number of processes of each order. This number is the process count of `Aar` only. No line tests that `Aao` has the same count. In the present facts.json both lists have 2 processes.
- The function `section4` continues after line 1041 with section 4.6.
